name: Uganda
snapshot: Yoweri Museveni, in power since 1986, won a seventh term in January 2026 against Bobi Wine, with his son and army chief positioned as heir.
culture: Uganda is home to the Buganda kingdom, whose kabaka still commands loyalty, and dozens of other peoples. Luganda, English and Swahili are widely spoken. Its vibrant music scene produced political stars like Bobi Wine, the "ghetto president". The source of the Nile at Jinja and mountain gorillas in Bwindi draw tourists.
society: Uganda has one of the world's youngest populations; most people were born after Museveni took power. It hosts more than 1.7 million refugees, mostly from South Sudan and Congo, with a progressive policy that lets them farm and work. Oil production around Lake Albert, with an export pipeline to Tanzania, is due to start. A 2023 anti-homosexuality law brought sanctions.
situation: Yoweri Museveni took power in 1986 after a five-year bush war, promising that the problem of Africa was leaders who overstayed. Forty years later, at 81, he won a seventh term.

The 15 January election gave him 71.65 percent, his strongest result in 30 years, against 24.72 percent for Robert Kyagulanyi, the singer-turned-politician known as Bobi Wine (GlobalSecurity). It was held under a nationwide internet blackout. During the campaign security forces fired tear gas and bullets at Wine's rallies; in a New Year's Eve speech Museveni urged police to use more tear gas on "the criminal opposition," saying it "doesn't kill." On election day soldiers raided Wine's home. He said he escaped and went into hiding, and at least seven people died in post-election clashes (Reuters via AllAfrica). Wine called the result fraud. The bigger question in Uganda is what comes after Museveni: his son, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, the army chief known for erratic social media posts, is widely seen as being prepared to succeed him. Uganda also has troops in South Sudan backing President Kiir.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years; term and age limits were removed in 2005 and 2017. The ruling National Resistance Movement dominates parliament, and the army is closely tied to the presidency.
holders: President Yoweri Museveni (NRM), in power since 1986.
